4. Mr. Md. Majibur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing for the accused petitioners submits, first, that there being only one eye witness in this case namely. P.W.4 Md. Kabir Ahmed Sardar, the son of the deceased and the other witnesses to whom he disclosed about seeing of the occurrence being all related to the deceased, the learned Judges of the High Court Division ought not to have relied on the evidence of P.W.4. He next submits that from the medical evidence on record it cannot be conclusively said that the death of deceased Jafar Ali Sardar was anti-mortem and homicidal in nature. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division ought to been drawn an adverse inference under Section 114 (g) of the Evidence Act for not examining some of the witnesses named in the charge-sheet. 

 5. The learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of evidence of P.W.4 Md. Kabir Ahmed Sardar believed that he was sleeping in the night of occurrence along with his father deceased Jafar Ali Sardar and saw the assault by the accused petitioners. The learned Judges further found that the night was a moon-lit night and but being open on all sides this witness had no difficulty in recognizing the accused persons. From the evidence of P.W.4 it appears that he was dragged by accused Mobarak and thrown out of the hut. He being frightened ran away to his house and narrated the occurrence to his cousins and he along with them returned and saw the dead body of deceased Jafar. The learned Judges not only believed the evidence of this eye witness, P.W.4. But also believed P.Ws. 3, 5, 6, 8 and 10 to whom this eye witness disclosed about the assault and named the accused persons. The learned Advocate could not point out any material discrepancies or omissions on a vital point for which this eye witness P.W.4 could be disbelieved; other than making a general submission that he being the solitary eye witness of the recognition of the accused persons should not have been relied upon. 

 6. From the medical evidence on record it also appears that deceased Jafar Ali Sardar died due to asphyxia as a result of pressure on the upper chest wall and neck and according to P.W.1 Dr. Md. Ishaque Ali, the injuries were anti-mortem and homicidal in nature. On consideration of the medical evidence on record, the learned Judges held that Jafar Ali Sardar was murdered in the night of occurrence and he did not die a natural death. 

 7. The learned Advocate for the petitioners could not show how the witnesses named in the charge-sheet were material witnesses in this case and for the non-examination of those witnesses adverse inference should be drawn under Section 114 (g) of the Evidence Act. The learned Judges did not consider those witnesses as material as there is only one eye witness in this case. Both the trial court and the learned Judges of the High Court Division having come to a conclusion of guilt of the accused persons after due consideration of the evidence on record, we do not think it necessary for us to reappraise the evidence afresh.
